subject: Dedicated capacity: follow-up + GPU band recommendation and $/1M token targets
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmerobotics.com>, Marcus Li <marcus.li@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-30T16:50:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity: follow-up + GPU band recommendation and $/1M token targets

Hi Olivia / Marcus — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a Dedicated SKU/quote: 

Summary of what I heard (please correct if I got anything wrong):
- Workload: real-time assistance + batch analytics for robot telemetry. Model family: Open-Transformer variant (~13B–70B range) with prompt/context sizes of 2–6k tokens; average generated tokens per request ~120, but heavy tails to 2k on long debug traces.
- Monthly token footprint (current pilot): ~40M tokens/month. Target production: 200M–1.2B tokens/month depending on adoption.
- Peak concurrency: 40 concurrent inference streams; typical per-stream throughput requirement ~250–800 tokens/sec depending on model size/latency SLAs.
- Latency SLO: median <120ms per token for interactive flows; batch analytics can tolerate higher latency.
- Budget signal: target blended unit cost $/1M tokens in the $75–$110 range for Dedicated (customer indicated ~$90/1M as aspirational).

Initial infrastructure read: given the model range and interactive latency requirement, two sensible bands we discussed:
1) H100-heavy band (recommended for 70B-ish variants + higher throughput): H100 80GB or 80GB HBM equivalent, NVLink-enabled, good for larger-context models and higher token/second. Estimated per-GPU sustained throughput (13B optimized -> ~1200 tokens/sec, 70B -> ~300–450 tokens/sec depending on quantization).
2) A100 80GB band (cost-efficient for 13B–30B variants and heavy quantization): lower unit cost but lower top throughput for the biggest variants.

Cost / unit-econ notes we touched on:
- Redwood Dedicated pricing will include reserved node commit + baseline throughput SLO. We can shape price to target ~$85–95 per 1M tokens for your expected mix with a 12 month commit at 4–8 H100-equivalent GPUs.
- Options to reduce unit cost: prefix/KV caching for repeated telemetry blobs, quantized model variants for lower-cost serving, and routing rules to direct non-interactive workloads to smaller/cheaper GPUs.

Suggested next steps (ordered):
1) Acme to share the sample token histogram (relative frequency by request size) and a one-week trace export — you mentioned Marcus can drop a CSV. (Marcus?)
2) Redwood (Camila + Ben) to produce a 3-band Dedicated SKU proposal: 1) Pilot (2 H100 equiv), 2) Prod-min (4 H100 equiv), 3) Prod-scale (8 H100 equiv) with price per million tokens, monthly commitment, and expected sustained throughput. I attached a draft SKU workbook for internal.
3) Quick joint deep-dive next week to validate throughput numbers on your real samples (we'll propose a 60–90 minute technical session with infra + ML engineer presence).
4) Tentative timeline: PO within 4–6 weeks after we align on numbers.

I'll loop Camila and Ben to take the SKU/throughput draft on and bring back a formal quote.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
viv@redwood.inference

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_sku_draft.xlsx (pricing + SKU bands), soc2_evidence_summary.pdf

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: follow-up + GPU band recommendation and $/1M token targets

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token profile: I exported an anonymized week of traffic and attached acme_token_profile.csv to this thread. The distribution is: ~60% short queries (<=150 tokens), ~30% mid (150–800), ~10% long traces (>800, up to ~2k).
- Pilot target: we want to run a 3-month pilot that hits ~200M tokens/month by month 3 (cloud trial suggests adoption ramp).
- Budget guardrails: procurement is looking at $80–$100 per 1M for the first year for Dedicated — flexibility if a 12-month commit lowers it.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence looks good — can you confirm retention windows and access logs for Private deployment?

Agree to the playbook you suggested. Marcus will drop the trace CSV now. Can we schedule the technical throughput session on Sep 3rd or Sep 4th? Our infra lead is available in the morning PT.

Olivia Chen
Director of AI Platform, Acme Robotics
olivia.chen@acmerobotics.com

On attachments: acme_token_profile.csv attached.
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>

Date: 2026-08-30T18:30:00Z
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity: follow-up + GPU band recommendation and $/1M token targets

Vivek / Ben — forwarding Acme's profile. Quick internal notes / asks so we can turn the draft SKU into a pricing delta: 

- Action: Ben, please run a ballpark throughput estimate per GPU for three model points (13B, 30B, 70B) using our optimized kernels and with and without 4-bit quantization. Include tokens/sec and expected concurrent streams per GPU.
- Action: I'll fill the pricing workbook with three committed term options (12/24/36 months) and show tiered $/1M tokens at each commit level and node count.
- Risk: long-tail requests (>800 tokens) will drive KV cache growth and memory pressure on 70B variants; add a fallback policy to route those to a slightly higher-latency batch lane to protect interactive SLAs.

Ben: Can you have the throughput slide + numbers by EOD tomorrow? I want to include it in the Sep 1st quote packet.

Thanks — Camila
